*PharmaCraft Daily - 24 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Thiazide diuretics act on the?
Ans: Distal convoluted tubule
Why: Thiazides inhibit the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule; used in hypertension.

🌍 *FMGE* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Amiloride is a potassium-sparing diuretic that blocks?
Ans: Epithelial sodium channels (ENaC)
Why: Amiloride and triamterene block ENaC in the collecting duct, sparing potassium (not via aldosterone).

🩺 *NEET PG* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Finerenone is a non-steroidal MRA used to reduce progression of?
Ans: Diabetic kidney disease
Why: Finerenone, a selective non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, slows diabetic CKD progression.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce CKD progression partly by?
Ans: Reducing intraglomerular hyperfiltration via tubuloglomerular feedback
Why: By increasing distal sodium delivery, SGLT2 inhibitors restore tubuloglomerular feedback, lowering hyperfiltration.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper III: Systemic)
Q: The drug of choice for absence seizures that also treats generalised seizures is?
Ans: Valproate
Why: Valproate is broad-spectrum (covers absence and generalised seizures); ethosuximide covers only absence.
